chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Safwan, from Ibn Muskhan, from Muhammad al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about jewelry (gold ornaments), is there zakat in it? He said, 'No.'

key_terms.أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah (Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq, peace be upon him)
key_terms.الْحُلِيِّ: Jewelry (specifically gold ornaments worn by women)

ai.seo_question: Is there zakat on gold jewelry according to Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies that gold jewelry (*al-huliy*) is exempt from obligatory zakat, a ruling that distinguishes it from gold held for commercial trade or savings. This exemption reflects the Shia scholarly view that personal adornment, provided it is not excessive or ostentatious, is not subject to the same wealth-circulation mandate as other assets. The narration underscores the practical application of zakat laws in distinguishing between utility and investment in personal wealth.
